title: constitution.md's Locked Stack section (and CLAUDE.md) still names Next.js 16 static export; the shipped frontend has been Vite since R7 (D6)
repro: Read .specify/memory/constitution.md 'Additional Constraints (Stack, Scope & Decision Authority)' and this project's own CLAUDE.md 'Stack' section (both say 'Next.js 16 (App Router, static export)' / 'Next.js 16 static export'), then read package.json: no "next" dependency anywhere; "scripts":{"dev":"vite","build":"vite build"}; devDependencies carry vite ^8.0.16 + @vitejs/plugin-react 6.0.1. There is a vite.config.ts and an index.html Vite entry point; components.json still declares "rsc": true and "css": "src/app/globals.css" (React-Server-Components / Next app-router settings that don't apply to a Vite SPA); src/app/page.tsx + src/app/globals.css are leftover Next-era files.
evidence: .specify/memory/constitution.md (Additional Constraints, 'Stack is locked: Tauri 2.x (Rust core) + Next.js 16 static export + React 19 + ...', read live this session), CLAUDE.md:16 ('Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router, static export) + React 19 + TypeScript'), package.json (no next dep; vite scripts; vite ^8.0.16, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.0.1), vite.config.ts:1-30, index.html, components.json (rsc:true, css:'src/app/globals.css'), src/app/page.tsx, docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md:28 D6 ('Vite migration verdict: zero blockers (1 next/font import, 2 app-shell files, no routing/SSR/API routes, vitest already Vite-based) ... change is surgical').
notes: Per this project's own Decision Authority tiers (constitution.md 'Additional Constraints' + CLAUDE.md 'Decision authority'), the Locked stack (BLUEPRINT §2) is Tier-1 and reversing it is Tier-4 — block-and-ask, record, never silent. The Next.js->Vite migration DID happen and WAS recorded (D6, R7 decision log) as a deliberate, low-risk, surgical change, but the Locked-stack PROSE in constitution.md and the Stack line in CLAUDE.md were never updated to match it — both currently, actively misdescribe the shipped framework. CLAUDE.md is loaded into every future Claude Code session on this project (including this one) as ground truth, so this isn't cosmetic: it primes every future contributor/agent with a wrong mental model of the rendering layer, App Router routing, RSC, etc. that don't exist in this codebase. Smallest fix: update constitution.md's Locked-stack line and CLAUDE.md's Stack line to 'Vite + React 19 (SPA, no SSR/RSC)', record the Next->Vite migration as the Tier-3/4 stack amendment it already was (cite D6), and clean up components.json (rsc:false, correct css path) + delete the leftover src/app/page.tsx + src/app/globals.css remnants.

title: External MCP surface exposes zero mutating capabilities — FR-021's 'same confirmation path' has no MCP-side implementation
repro: Every read_only=False ('host_action') capability in catalog.py (open_panel, set_chart_symbol, open_company_overview, set_chart_indicators, add_to_watchlist, propose_order, close_panel, focus_panel, portfolio_add_position, portfolio_update_position, portfolio_delete_position, write_note, remove_from_watchlist, save_layout, save_screen, set_region) leaves `mcp` at its dataclass default (False) — none is ever passed mcp=True. Call any of them over the external MCP surface -> mcp_capabilities() (catalog.py:1496-1503, filters on c.mcp) never listed it as a tool in the first place, and even a direct services.agent_tools.invoke_tool('portfolio_add_position', {...}) call raises KeyError (no register_tool call for any host_action id exists anywhere in the codebase) -> mcp_server._make_catalog_tool's except clause returns {'ok': False, 'error': "tool 'portfolio_add_position' is not available in this build"}.
evidence: sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:962-1456 (16 host_action capabilities, `mcp` left at the dataclass default False at catalog.py:93,118), sidecar/services/agent_tools/catalog.py:1496-1503 (mcp_capabilities() filters strictly on c.mcp), sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:106-124 (_make_catalog_tool dispatches to agent_tools.invoke_tool; KeyError -> {'ok': False, ...}), sidecar/services/agent_tools/__init__.py:62-67 (invoke_tool's KeyError path for an unregistered id), sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1190-1225 (_make_host_action — the ONLY code path that actually stages a reviewable diff for a host_action tool call, registered per-run into the internal SSE chat loop's local tool table; mcp_server.py never touches it).
notes: Constitution II ('one capability catalog, many consumers... a capability MUST NOT exist for only one consumer') and US5/FR-020-022 ('an external agent... drives the SAME capabilities the built-in copilot uses', 'the read_only flag MUST drive both the internal mutation gate and the external MCP read-only annotation') describe a mutation surface that is reachable-but-gated for an external MCP client, mirroring the internal diff/accept flow. What ships is a mutation surface that is simply invisible to MCP — safe by omission, but not the promised parity, and it means 'Vysted as an MCP framework' (the stated moat, per README/US5) is read-only-only today for anything beyond quotes/charts/screener/fundamentals/news/portfolio-READ. Smallest fix: either opt the host_action capabilities into mcp=True behind a host-side proposal queue an external client can create-and-poll (mirroring proposed-changes.ts's accept/reject shape), or narrow FR-021/US5's wording to state MCP is read-only-only for v1 so the gap is a documented decision, not a silent one.

title: All-providers-failed data errors reach the REST/panel layer as raw Python exception strings, never an honest 'needs a key' / 'what would unlock it' message
repro: Every provider fails for a symbol (e.g. GET /quotes/ZZZQNOPE against the isolated sidecar) -> the global ProviderError handler (sidecar/app.py) turns it into a 502 whose body is str(exc) verbatim -> the calling panel (equity-overview / watchlist / chart) renders err.message as-is. Live: GET :52152/quotes/ZZZQNOPE -> 502 {"detail":"yfinance quote failed for 'ZZZQNOPE': 'PriceHistory' object has no attribute '_dividends'"} (reproduced by the prior session-2 chunk, re-verified this session at sidecar/app.py:312-315).
evidence: sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:428-440 (all-null shell never served; last ProviderError raised, so a genuine all-fail case DOES reach the caller as an exception, not a fabricated 200), sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:104-115 (429/404 humanized, everything else falls through to a bare 502 detail=str(exc)), sidecar/app.py:312-315 (verified at current HEAD: `JSONResponse(status_code=502, content={"detail": str(exc)})`), sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:65 (raw exception text embedded into the message the registry ultimately raises), src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:763, src/modules/watchlist/WatchlistPanel.tsx:206, src/modules/chart/ChartPanel.tsx:408 (each prints err.message verbatim, no fallback copy). Contrast the AGENT leg, which already has a closed, human reason vocabulary: sidecar/services/agent_tools/fundamentals.py:23-51 (rate_limited / not_found / provider_error).
notes: Constitution VIII ('surfacing an honest, human unavailable — naming what would unlock it — only when every configured source has failed') and spec.md's Edge Cases (both the general list and the Pass-B list, INT-SP-51/84/91 all name this exact case) promise the SYSTEM does this, not just the agent tool leg. The gap is real and reachable from ordinary use (any thinly-covered or delisted symbol on a keyless install). This is the same underlying defect as INT-spec-90-1 (docs/redesign/verification/r15/census/raw/intent-spec-90.json) — filed again here (against the same evidence, re-verified at current HEAD) because it independently blocks INT-SP-51 and INT-SP-84 in THIS chunk; the Gate-2 merge step should dedupe the two raw ids onto one register entry. Smallest fix: route provider_registry's all-fail ProviderError through the existing services/errors.py humanizer (already used for LLM/provider-chat errors per D43) before it reaches app.py's exception handler, and have it carry a `hint` field ('needs an EODHD/Twelve Data key' / 'symbol not covered by any installed provider') that the three panels render instead of err.message.
